Another place recommended in the Michelin guide.

It lays at the end of a narrow alley. Since its recommendation it had to expand. Now there are two Restaurants which pretty much sit next to each other. Thanks to that we did not have to wait for a table of 5.

You take a seat at small wooden tables and sit on small wooden stool. The choice of dishes is pretty overwhelming. Luckily the michelin recommended dishes were marked.

I myself had the beef skewers which were great. You have to roll the skewer with vermicelli, greens and pickles into a salad leaf. A typicall Vietnamesen dish.

The most interesting dish though was the fried pork. The breading was so uniquely thick that you could hear the crunch through the whole Restaurant. Also the breading had something sweet about it. MICHELIN - Vietnamese Street Food
Dec 2024 • Solo
Another Michelin find in Saigon: a local Vietnamese restaurant specialising in Vietnamese street food, this time hidden in an alley way near Ben Thanh Market in D1. 

I don’t know why there is any negative reviews for this place! I, just like most people who have eaten here, really enjoyed everything i ordered: the Seafood Bánh xèo was prefect. the spring rolls tasty, the fresh watermelon juice refreshing. 

I have been coming to Saigon for over 15 years and I am currently living in D9. I have had a lot of Bánh xèo of varying qualities over those years and this one, today was spot on: not overdone crispy or oily … just perfect with the right amount of stuffing. I would go back just to eat this dish. 

I personally think as I normally do, avoid the negative people and go and taste it for yourself and make up your own mind. The price is still ridiculously good value for the size of servings.

One of the best Vietnamese dinners
Aug 2023 • Couples
My husband and I had dinner in this restaurant, complete with a mention in the Michelin guide
ENVIRONMENT: the restaurant is inside a gallery, where there are also other restaurants, so don't get confused. Part of the restaurant, however indoors and outdoors and part indoors with a first floor where we had dinner. Wooden tables, paper placemats and everything with the place of the place. The floor where we dined was well furnished, with tables even though we dined on a sofa. The sideboard is also beautiful. Air-conditioned room. Partly open kitchen
SERVICE: fast staff who speaks English since the customers are all tourists and the menu is also in English.
FOOD: all very good, good quality raw materials, well-made and well-presented preparations. Wide choice on the menu of courses which ranged from rice to the delicious bánh xèo or Vietnamese rice flour pancakes fried in a pan and stuffed with meat and prawns. The salad with small courgettes, the meat, the rice with coconut and prawns are good. Liked the dessert less.
QUALITY/PRICE RATIO: Being a place for tourists, prices may be higher than other places, always for the same target, but I admit that the quality of the raw materials was really better than many other places where we had eaten.
OVERALL OPINION: Absolutely recommended!

Located down a small street near Ben Thanh Market in Ho Chi Minh City, Bếp Mẹ Ỉn (which translates to “Mom’s Kitchen”) is a hidden gem. Here’s why you should consider dining here:

Tasty Vietnamese Flavors:
Bếp Mẹ Ỉn serves up authentic Vietnamese cuisine that bursts with flavor. From deep-fried tofu with impeccably crispy exteriors to succulent grilled chicken legs, your taste buds are in for a treat.
Fantastic Price Value:
If you’re looking for a budget-friendly meal without compromising on quality, this is the place. Bếp Mẹ Ỉn offers a wide variety of dishes at wallet-friendly prices.
Friendly Staff:
The staff here are warm, friendly, and attentive. Whether you’re a local or a traveler, they’ll make you feel right at home.
Refreshing Drinks and Desserts:
Pair your meal with interesting and refreshing drinks. And don’t forget to explore their dessert options—they’re delightful!
Pro Tip: Try the Grilled Chicken Leg with Chilli Salt and thank me later!

BEP ME IN
Apr 2024 • Friends
Up to this point, we had really only been eating street food or at hyper local spots recommended by tour guides, so it was nice to eat somewhere that had actual chairs as opposed to those tiny little plastic stools ahaha. I do love a meal on a plastic stool don't get me wrong though...

We came here for dinner after a long day at the Cu Chi Tunnels and fresh off a 3L tower of beer split between the 2 of us, so we were pretty toasted ahaha. We entered through an alley where locals were chillin shirtless on their motorbikes rippin cigs, hung a right and were met with a pretty long line.

After 10 minutes we were seated, and handed a menu. I scanned the room and was a little disappointed as it was mostly tourists and only a handful of locals... but I had to catch myself writing that just now because I literally am a tourist ahahah.

The menu was HUGE, filled with pictures which is always a nice touch especially when data is LIMITED to look online. We opted to get a feast as we were STARVING. We ended up ordering 7 different items and some beer to keep the train rolling.

When we finished ordering, I could feel this german couple laughing at us for the sheer amount of food we got. After about 5 minutes the guy leaned over and said "So you got all 7?" in a hella snarky tone. Like bro mind ya business, stop pocket watching. Worry about yourself and... nvm I'm not gonna be mean on here.

The food, while 3-4x (~$8USD per entree) the price of some of the more local spots, was on par with anything we had on our trip, and likely 1.5x the portion. BIG DAWG PORTION SIZES!

Our favorites were the Banh Xe, the Bo Lui, Com Tam Suon, and that fried rice in a coconut. The Bo Lui was definitely leading the charge though, those beef skewers with the rice vermicelli had been blessed by the gods.

Service wasn't the best, as I had to ask for a napkin 2 different times before I just got up and grabbed some from an adjacent table, but idk I'm not gonna be a Karen and knock a star off for that lol they were busy af in here.

A popular cosy restaurant
Dec 2023 • Couples
This restaurant was recommended by our guide when we first arrived in Saigon. We went there on our first evening, and then back again for lunch on our final day. It is situated down a narrow alleyway but we found it easily with the instructions given by our guide. (He mentioned that this was his 'go to' restaurant when he was going for a meal with friends.) The restaurant is small and you will generally have to share one of the long tables with other people. You may also need to wait to be seated, though on both occasions the wait was no more than ten minutes (after initially being told that it could be half an hour). However, it is worth it as the food is very good, albeit a bit more expensive than in some other establishments. (And note that the menu price does not include tax which adds 8% to the bill.)

Boston, Massachusetts267 contributions
0
Super Yummylicious
May 2019 • Friends
This “insider” spot is hidden in a small alley near the market place. The small alley leading in are lined with manicure shops that are out in the open (you sit on a small plastic teeny weenie stool and they do manicures on the road for you). So if google map tells you that way, don’t worry you are headed in the right direction! 
Once we got there it was very crowded. Most of the crowd are foreigners though, I don’t recall seeing any locals. However the food is super delicious and they are quite authentic. Highly recommend the coconut fried rice, there are shaved and bits of actual coconut amidst the rice, so there’s a strong kick of coconut with every bite. Not a very usual combination that you get elsewhere. 
Another signature dish is the Vietnamese style egg pancake. SO GOOD. It looked much plainer than it actually tastes, the look doesn’t do it justice. It’s served on a huge woven basket platter (also very Instagram-worthy), and there’s either seafood filling version, or you could get plain veggie filling version which is just as good and cheaper. You wrap it in fresh green leaves, and each bite is super flavourful.

This the one. Go now.
Dec 2018 • Family
136 Le Thanh Ton street. A small alley leads you into a few restaurants and shops, it’s on the right, with a bike in the entrance... find it. GO GO GO.
Beautiful place , room upstairs. We got there early for us , 6.45pm. so glad we did. Every minute people walked out of the allly and was looking for a seat . We had a great outside spot. Very friendly and welcoming staff , plenty of time allowed to chat before we ordered . No pressure , a very relaxed environment. Kim our waitress said once we were ready to wave , catch her eye and she’d come. 

So starters , pancakes , pork and shrimp , nothing new there , but it’s the little details, very tasty wine vinegar dip with garlic and chillis, may not have been that but it was a great addition to the pancake, which was large and crispy and full of filling. Great bed of lettuce to munch on as well. Sprring rolls with shrimp and pork , beautifully seasoned and same dip , two dishes plenty big enough , three of us sharing. A very fine shredded cabbage , maybe a little onion on the sides , I scoffed it all down and I’m not a veg girl normally. 
So mains. Pork with green peppercorns and chilli in a clay pot. I could eat this again right now as I write this . Good portion of meat , lovely rich sauce , great flavours .Veg fried rice with coconut served in a coconut . Very delicate and fragrant. Pork ribs on a bed of straw. You can’t eat the straw , but the shredded veg under is very edible. Plant of food. We thought it was the best so far , but we’ve only just arrived. Three scoops of lime / lemon sorbet , I know it says it’s icecream but it’s not. It’s very fresh and it’s sorbet. 
Starters, mains, and pudding , few beers and bill is a bit more than we’ve paid , but I’d say it’s soooooooooo worth it. The taste and smells , the presentation the wow in your mouth is worth it. The staff are Uber caring and genuine with their time. It was a 1st meal with our daughter who arrived from uk. Go. You will be well looked after. 
I thank you BepMe In for your staff and hospitality.

Lovely staff, great food
Aug 2018 • Family
We had to look for a while to find this restaurant, which is hidden from the busy streets of Ho Chi Min City. 

We ordered a local draft beer as soon as we sat down, because we were extremely thirsty. This first glass of beer tasted very good and was a very promising start of a lovely dinner experience. 

We ordered some dishes to share and they arrived very quickly. Often this is an indication of non-fresh food, but this was definitely not the case this time! The food tasted amazing and was definitely cooked fresh. 

We especially loved the pork ribs with lime leaves which came with an awesome dipping sauce. We have experienced that the dipping sauces here in Vietnam quite often overpower the overall flavor of a dish. This dipping sauce however complemented the seasoning of the beef perfectly and really enhanced the flavor of the lime leaves. 

Finally the service was wonderful as well. The staff was very kind and attentive. We left the restaurant with a very good feeling and started a nice evening walk at the local market located close to the restaurant. After a few minutes one of the waiters came running from the restaurant towards us with the key of our hotel room in his hands. It apparently slipped out of our wallet when we were paying for the lovely meal. The waiter must have searched for us quite intensively because it was very busy and we were quite far from the restaurant already! We were very grateful for this act of kindness from the waiter and leaving this good review is the least I can do in return! 5 stars very well deserved in my opinion!

Great find in an amazing city
Apr 2018 • Friends
For my first visit to Vietnam I wanted to make sure that I avoided the usual tourist trap locations. This small restaurant in the back streets of Saigon was a superb introduction to Vietnamese dining for me and my friends and it felt more authentic than anything else I had seen on the main streets. The menu was simple but varied. I opted for the pork and noodle dish with spring rolls. The food was served quickly and it was delicious. The service was excellent and the staff were very friendly and always had a smile on their faces. The restaurant is quite small but even so we did not need a reservation. It would seat maybe 25 people. The tables were shared which was a nice touch.

I would highly recommend this restaurant to anybody visiting the city of Ho Chi Minh.

Amazing food and lovely place
Apr 2018 • Couples
We have just had an absolutely amazing dinner at Bep Me In. We went on the strength of the food reviews and we are so glad we did. 

We started with rice paper rolls with pork, which were really fresh and tasty, with a nice dipping sauce and side salad. For our main course we shared the tamarind prawns, which had a beautifully balanced sour, sweet and savoury flavour, and the caramelised pork, which was incredibly tender and meaty. We had some coconut and vegetable fried rice on the side, which had a lovely delicate coconut flavour. Everything was piping hot, perfect portion sizes and so, so tasty. We rounded off with a coconut ice cream affogato, which was the perfect end to the meal. We chose a carafe of chilled red to go with the meal, and it was a really good match.

The restaurant is quirky with really interesting decor; the staff were attentive and helpful, and the menu gave plenty of choice without being overwhelming.

We are really tempted to go back and repeat the whole lot again tomorrow. It came to about 650,000 dong, which we thought was great value for three courses with wine.

Warm Welcome from Chaulita
Mar 2018 • Couples
We so enjoyed our meal last year at Bep Me In, we thought we'd go back again this year. We are so glad we did. The manager of the restaurant, Chau, came to greet us and we told her we were back for the second year in a row. She was so thrilled, she made us a dessert that she grew up eating - banana with ice cream and peanuts.

The restaurant is located in an alley near the Benh Thahn Market, and so worth searching for (as are most gems in Saigon). Fortunately, because we were repeat diners, we knew what we were looking for.

Our table was out on the street in the alley and although there is not much of a view, you are not there for the view, but for the food. I had one of Chau's favorite dishes - shrimp in coconut rice, and my husband had cold noodles with beef. We shared the steamed mixed vegetables with caramelized fish sauce, which immediately took us back to our trip to Phu Quoc - so spicy and tasty.

If you're in the area, check this place out!

Busy & trendy, but food is a little sanitised!
Jan 2018 • Couples
My wife and I dropped in here while in Saigon, staying just around the block at the Silverlands Hotel. The first night we dropped by (Monday night), the place was completely full, so we ate elsewhere (see terrible review of Quan Cu'a Tay restaurant!).
We return on the Tuesday night and managed to squeeze into a space on benches between other couples (I think an Ausie couple and a Scandinavian couple?).
I had the Grilled/BBQ Pork with noodles, which comes with a pile of fresh herbs & green salad. It was fine, but it wasn't filling (more of everything please!). My wife went for the Chicken Pho (or equivalent), a bowl of noodles with some nice chunks of poached chicken, alongside some bean sprouts and herbs. My wife seemed to enjoy hers and she found her dish quite filling. I tasted her chicken which was good, but nothing special. The prices here are at least 3 times what you would pay from a street vendor. I wouldn't bother again, I would go elsewhere and get a decent helping of tastier food at a much cheaper price!

Fresh, friendly, delicious
Feb 2018 • Family
We saw the good reviews for this place on TA so we (2 adults, 2 children aged 9 and 11) walked here for dinner. The place is not really easy to find (being up a lane) but once you enter the lane Ben Me In and a few other restaurants appear.

Staff at BMI were friendly and helpful from the moment we arrived. We were ushered to a table and ordered and received drinks immediately. The iced passion fruit juice was sublime. We got excellent help and recommendations for food, and it arrived really quickly. Wait staff were friendly, attentive and professional without being imposing. You could tell they knew what they were doing and had a real interest in their customers. They spoke English well.

The food was fresh and delicious. The Vietnamese pancake was one of the best I’ve had, and the spring rolls can’t go without a mention. So good we ordered a second serve! The children enjoyed the grilled chicken, and fried rice. Chicken Pho was excellent (you can always tell straight away by the quality of the soup).

The food was really excellent for the price. Not super cheap Vietnamese street food, but certainly not expensive given the quality.

I would definitely eat here again, regularly if I had the chance.

Bep Me In... Feed Me More!
Nov 2017 • Friends
The service was great: fast, efficient and our server spoke wonderful English.

We ordered a whole heap of food: at no point did we feel disappointed. 

The fried tofu with two sauces was recommended and a definitely must try. Crisp exterior with a melt in your mouth interior. 

The pho was also delicious and nicely presented. Our server taking over with the condiments and showing us how it’s to be eaten in try Vietnamese fashion.

The grilled beef skewers with banh hoi noodles was my clear favourite with our ever helpful server showing is how to eat it properly.

We also decided to try the wing bean stir fry only because it’s not a vegetable I get back home and we were not disappointed: crunchy and pleasant to taste... I personally could’ve just sat there and ate another plate.

As for drinks, the salty lemon drink was 
my favourite - something unique and refreshing about sweet and salty and sour with every mouthful.

Definitely worth a sojourn down the side alley to visit. The other reviews are right: it had a touristy feel but you didn’t get that feeling that it was inauthentic. Enjoy!

Great food friendly staff
Sep 2017 • Friends
Presentation is very nice. You can tell the manager (Chau) really cares about her restaurant and the dining experience for her customers. We chatted with her for probably 20 minutes and she gave us great tips on Vietnamese phrases, how to bargain, asked for feedback on the food. She cares a lot about her craft and knows that people read reviews online and works to make sure that this restaurant is successful. You will likely have a very good meal here.

Slightly hard to find. Google maps shows it as street facing. Across the street from the market there's an alley that opens in to a courtyard, above the alley is a small rectangular white sign with a red and yellow logo of a man eating noodles and the words "bep me in" in a modern font. It's not a very big sign! Look for alleys and then look for a white sign attached to the wall of the alley.

Decor is nice, there's a 3d art thing on the wall of a lady riding a bike. Very clean. I prefer western style chicken dishes, I got the lotus flower chicken dish, it was awesome. Girlfriend got the shrimp soup in a clay pot with crunchy things (i'm not so good with food names). She said it was awesome. Portions are definitely asian sized, if you're a hefty american (like reviewer A8889A) you're going to want to order a side of steamed rice. Between the lotus flower chicken, steamed rice and egg rolls I had a pretty satisfying meal and i'm 170lbs (77kg). Two meals, two sides of rice, four beers and the egg rolls, plus desert put us back about 445,000 dong or $20 usd but you could definitely eat there cheaper. Main appetizers are about 90,000 dong ($4.50) and beers are 30,000 dong ($1.50)

Restaurant is very very clean, service was fast and nice, good food, great prices. 2 minute walk from the market makes it a great choice for backpackers.

Great authentic Vietnamese food
Sep 2017 • Couples
My wife and I have just returned from having dinner at Bep Me In located down a small alley opposite the Ben Thanh Market on Le Thanh Ton. We went there because of the great reviews on Trip Advisor.

I ordered two mixed egg pancakes (one each) which I thought was an entrée as other restaurants around Vietnam had them as a small dish. How wrong was I. The waitress saw my eyes open very wide when they arrived as they were a huge dish by themselves. The pancakes contained chicken, prawns and bean shoots. They were accompanied by traditional Asian green salad leaves and a small bowl of sweet chilli sauce.

I also ordered the traditional beef Pho which was also tasty but could have done without because of the size of the pancake.

The service was good, staff and friendly and keen to have a chat. When the bill came out it was for for 430,000 Dong which we thought was reasonable as it also included two drinks (about $25 AUS). On leaving, the manager chased us down as she realised she gave us the wrong bill as were were only supposed to be charged 330,000 Dong ($19). She refunded us the 100,000 dong less our tip. How's that for honesty!

Anyway, we highly recommend this little eatery.

Enjoy! Cheers, Paul

Fresh and tasty food, lovely service
Jul 2017 • Couples
Being tucked away in an alley, it’s not a place you would ‘stumble across’ but there is well lit signage on the street so it’s certainly not difficult to find. It’s a small space with cute and quirky interior design making it feel like you’re sitting in an old fashioned market type restaurant. Bench seating is comfortable, the main room is air conditioned and spotlessly clean. Staff are super friendly and helpful with suggestions if required. We opted for the zucchini flowers stuffed with basa fish (delicate and tasty), pork in pepper and caramel (delicious!) and Vietnamese pizza. The pizza was the standout for me – a large prawn cracker type base with a soft rice paper wrapper to cover and toppings (pork, bean sprouts, egg, etc) over that. The texture and flavours were well chosen and beautifully balanced. We also had crunchy spring rolls which were pleasant but not as impressive as the other dishes. Refreshments include beer and wine by the glass. Prices are very realistic, in fact our total came to only 395,000. I would go again.

Best Meal in Vietnam
Jul 2017 • Couples
My husband and I have been traveling through Vietnam for the past two weeks on our honeymoon. Tonight was our last night in Vietnam, and my husband wanted to have one more authentic meal here.

This place is nondescript, cozy, and hidden in an alley, but we did not have any difficulty finding it. We were seated and waited on by the owner himself, J.C. My husband has a shellfish allergy, and J.C. took the time to sit down with him and pick out safe items that he could eat. He recommended the winged green beans, garlic rice, and grilled pork. Every item was delicious and packed with flavor. The beans were cooked in garlic and butter, the garlic rice was served in a red clay pot, and the pork was grilled to perfection. We ate every bite and sent back empty plates - this is the first meal in Vietnam that we have completely finished. For dessert, we enjoyed coconut flan served in a coconut shell. We shared a light, refreshing Platinum beer to drink - we had not seen this beer served anywhere else during our trip. 

I would highly recommend this place to anyone traveling thru Ho Chi Minh City. If you're staying at the Rex Hotel, this is an easy walk. If you're not, it's worth going out of your way to come eat here. Per the owner, "taste is paramount" and you will not regret eating here.

Excellent Street food but not street food
May 2017 • Couples
A little off the main thorough fare and tucked in the furthest corner of a back lane. 
We arrived past 9pm and were the only customers. It was decorated to be reminiscent of dining on the street but it was clean and quiet with staff that spoken good English. 
The menu was interesting and everything we ordered was truly delicious. 
We had the rice paper pizza which was crispy and unique and very interesting- yummy. 
We also had grilled beef which was very tasty but the best dish was the grilled pork - 2 cuts were presented beautifully, belly and loin and both were heavenly especially dipped in the funky shrimp paste. 
Toilet was clean and fragrantly scented with lemon grass and good quality individual hand towels were provided. 
Deserves it high rating on TA.

63 contributions

Perfection
May 2017 • Family
I had dinner here with my wife and daughter. We have only been in Vietnam three nights, but this was our favorite meal so far. Each dish was fresh and packed with a kaleidoscope of flavours. 

Fried spring rolls with rafter fish and peanuts: packed with fish and peanuts (a wonderful twist), served with a delicious mini-salad on the side.

Morning glory with garlic: not to be missed by garlic lovers. This spinach like vegetable was silky smooth with loads of soft garlic, melt in the mouth perfection.

Stewed tofu with mushrooms: the simple name for this understates the unctuous flavours that come through.

Pork cooked with green peppercorns and chili sauce: my dish of the night. Nice, subtle bite of green peppercorns, a hint of fresh chili and tender pork.

Fried rice with garlic: again, a dish far better than its humble name with wonderful bits of crisp garlic scattered through the moist rice, fried to perfection without any hint of greasiness.

Great value and pleasant service.

Cheap and cheerful
Feb 2017
Not as hard to find as some reviews make out so don't let this discourage you from going - we found it with no trouble, just as per the location map so do look at that before heading out. Look out for the logo, it's right at the start of the alley way.

There is shared seating e.g one long bench that probably fits 6 people on a table and they try to seat you apart so this didn't bother us, we had enough privacy as one needs for a quick lunch. It's very basic decor but has fans and light AC which makes it pleasant and it's clean. Can even put your bag on a hook so it's not on the floor! 

The food we ordered was scrumptious, I'm not quite sure why we don't get this style of food easily in the uk. Highly recommend the pork and shrimp pancake, the dipping sauce is divine. A little hard to eat but ok if you fold and use your hands! Also loved the garlic rice, you need to really LOVE garlic to fully appreciate. 2 drinks and 5 yummy dishes came to £16 - I'd definitely go again if in HCMC.

Could have been a 5 stars...
Jan 2017 • Couples
It's not easy to write this review. 
The place is nice, clean and the staff is lovely however you cannot run out of 50% of your menu at 8pm. When we reached the place at 8.30 we had to wait a little bit to get the table but around 8.50 we were in.
When we started to order the waiter pointed us the dishes they had already run out and after placing the order another lovely lady came back saying that most part of our choices were finished too. I know that there is some people who eat quite early (6.30-7pm) but at 8pm you cannot have finished half of your menu. They run out of spring rolls(fried and fresh), morning glory, pork caramelized, pork bamboo, a kind of pho..and other few dishes.
I can accept the fact: "it s new years" or "part of staff is on holiday" but at least you should have been honest from the beginning explaining the situation.At the end we had 2 beers and only 1 crispy noodles as my girlfriend wanted to try it. 
As gesture of goodwill they offered us complimentary drinks, however I would have preferred to have dinner rather than a beer at 10pm.
I would like to take this opportunity to invite the manager to point what is on the menu or not in order to avoid unpleasant surprises (Especially because other tables around us had the same problem and basically have been forced to order the last portions available). AThe place was nice and I was excited to try it ... but I could not eat in a restaurant at 8pm.

Delicious Vietnamese Food, with a touch of Artsy Class
Jan 2017 • Couples
My husband and I came here for dinner, luckily we did a little research ahead of time because it was down a nondescript alley and would have been hard to find if we hadn't known! It was nice to be off the crazy Ben Thanh market area and at a calmer spot. So down the nail salon alley we went to arrive at Bep Me In. The owner is French and the foot is Vietnamese deliciousness. No locals were eating there, but it didn't matter because the food was so tasty. It was like a little more artsy/classy than Vietnam street food, but just as (if not more) appetizing. We ordered the pork on bamboo (our favorite!), coconut rice (really great flavor!), and fried spring rolls (fried goodness). The three dishes were just the right amount of food and variation to create an excellent dinner. The owner stopped by our table to make sure our dinner was good, and the wait staff were friendly and kind. A great experience! Highly recommend.

Over expecting food and service
Jan 2017 • Friends
I was been here a few times already, and I always have good feeling about the foods and service.
The service from waiters, waitresses and manager are really good, they smiled all the time and be really patient to explained all our questions.
Fried Tofu is really over our expecting, crispy but soft inside, seasame offers the good smelling in this dish. My friends and I are meat lover, but in here that we can be tofu lover!
BBQ pork is really amazing, the meat is cooked quite well, juicy and tender but still is firm texture when you bite it. With some lemongrass you won't feel too heavy after several pieces.
Deep fried vegetables are quite good, it's a traditional fried vegetable style in our Asian culture. Garlic with some oil then deep fried with vegetables or some meats. Every time I will order at least one dish of vegetable.
My favorite dish is fried rice!!!
They use whole coconut stewed shrimps and rice.when you eat it, you can feel the real coconut flavor inside.
garlic fried rice is incredible, only garlic and rice but the rice is a little bits crispy. If you order some meats or tofu with sauce, you can put some sauce with rice. That's delectable!!!!
It's hard to write all dishes which I've tried and want to let more people know... so just write a several dishes.
Thanks Bep Me In, my friend and I will still go your there often and try all dishes from you!

Much ado about.... tiny portions
Aug 2016 • Friends
This restaurant is a very good example of how tripadvisor can make an ordinary thing sound great. Congratulations tripadvisor :) The hundreds of the reviews were partially at least the result of the big sign at the entrance to the restaurant asking customers to write their opinion on tripadvisor. (By the way: A good idea!) At arrival, we were cordially welcome by the CHARMING owner/host (?) and asked to wait a few minutes as we did not have a reservation. The decor of this small restaurant is nice but nothing extraordinary, and the long tables resemble communal rooms where you eat side by side with other guests; nice for a group of friends, but not necessarily for a romantic date. After some problems with communication – the waitresses are really nice, but at least some of them need brushing up on English food vocabulary - we ordered soup: Pho bo tai thap and Bun thang (cost 35 000 each). Pho was quite good (more limejuice would be welcome though), but Bun thang was not good at all and resembled salted water with a few blant tasting pieces of meat….. And then came the second course dishes: carmelised pork Thit kho caramel and spareribs Suon non la truc. And surprise surprise…. Last time I saw such small portions was in a fusion restaurant…. 3 (three) small bones with hardly any meat on were presented as spareribs (cost 105 000!) and 4 pieces of mostly fat meat as caramelised pork (cost 80 000). Rice or noodles not included. As for taste, the meat was quite good, if a litle too salty. For desert we had quite a big portion of icecream, which really was sorbet (cost105 000) and, again, a mere MORSEL of pretty tasty banana cake (cost 50 000). To sum up, I was not impressed by the food at all, and will rather go to a different restaurant for my next meal….

Delicious Local Vietnamese Street Food
Nov 2016 • Friends
First proper dinner in Vietnam and colleagues brought us to Bep Me In - a quaint little eatery tucked away in a rustic corner, down a little alley where i thought I could squeeze in a mani-pedi after dinner. 

The drinks specialty of preserved fruits was refreshing with the preserved plum drink being a favorite at our table. The drinks were assembled in a make-shift stall that resembled a small utilities van in a previous life. The wall art was reminiscent 

Once the drinks were settled, the feasting began with a whole host of wonderfully, tasty, delicious foods beginning with a pancake looking thing that we wrapped in rice paper rolls and Vietnamese herbs. 

A stir fried beef served in a hollowed out bamboo stem was divine which was quickly followed up with spring rolls and rice paper rolls - both of which are unlike what I'd typically get back home in Melbourne, Australia (notwithstanding living near one of the largest Vietnamese precincts around there). The fish cakes were served, cut in wedge-shapes, like a flat pancake... it didn't taste anything like any fish cake I've had (thank you, Thailand - you've spoiled me). 

But the best part was the grilled pork (two types, no less) served with rice noodles, Vietnamese herbs and a sweet-sour dressing that gets poured over the ingredients before hunger (and greed) take over and you scoff it down. 

A most satisfying meal full of wonder and awe and simplicity... one that could ruin the experience I used to have of loving Vietnamese food back home.

A Hidden Gem...
Aug 2016 • Solo
I picked up a card for their restaurant at Une Journee a Paris and put it into my pocket a few weeks ago. Today, I wanted to go to Ben Thanh to buy flowers not too far from their premises. The taxi stopped in front of the alley that leads to the courtyard in which the restaurant is located. As you pass through the alley, you may be tempted to have a manicure, pedicure, or foot massage, but don't put off the amazing dining experience you about to enjoy. This is an establishment that has set out to do everything right. The decor is fun. The service impeccable. I have only been once, but I am going back as soon as I can to show my wife the amazing stuff they serve. I had the the tofu smothered in sesame seeds with two dips as an appetizer. Beautiful. My lunch was the frog's legs in lemon grass and herbs with slices from a baguette. Absolutely delicious.
As I was eating two French girls came in who seemed familiar with the staff. We chatted a bit about the place....being a gray haired old guy,I am a safe chat, and we agreed that this was a gem. In fact, they said it was the best place they eaten in Viet Nam. Please, walk down that alley and try their food. You will be so glad you did.
